points.label: The lane and the gate: a steep lane ends at an iron gate with a rusted chain (rusted through) and a sign: Radio Larkhaven. Private. (a way in and out)
A gap in the fence by the observatory path (a way in and out)
The cable trench, from the observatory grounds (a way in and out)
The steep bank down into the gardens of the big houses (a way out only: too steep to climb up, easy to slide down)
The transmitter hut: brick, boarded windows. Inside: racks of dead valves, a desk, a 1926 logbook, thick cables running out and up the tower
The yard: gravel and nettles round the tower's four concrete feet. Steel guy wires hum, though there is no wind
The tower: a steel lattice mast with a caged ladder, a platform halfway up and a platform at the top
Six glowing valves hang from the old aerial at the top, wired together. This is where he sings
The cable trench: covered, it runs from the hut, under the fence, into the observatory grounds
